make.name: Chevrolet
make.description: General Motors' mass-market brand. Its EVs run from the original Spark EV and Bolt EV to the Ultium-based Equinox EV, Blazer EV and Silverado EV and the 2027 Bolt; outside North America it also sells China-built EVs such as the Spark EUV and Captiva EV. Chevrolet stopped selling new cars in China in August 2026.

models.name: Spark EV
models.description: Battery-electric version of the Spark city car, built in South Korea and sold in limited numbers (mainly California and Oregon, later Maryland, plus South Korea and Canadian fleets) from 2013 to 2016. It was GM's first retail battery EV and was replaced by the Bolt EV.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Five-door city car with an 82-mile EPA range; the 2015 model year switched from an A123 lithium-iron-phosphate pack to a smaller LG Chem pack with the same range.

models.name: Bolt
models.description: Chevrolet's affordable long-range EV. The first-generation Bolt EV hatchback (2017-2023, also sold in Europe as the Opel Ampera-e) ended production in December 2023; a second-generation Bolt, a small crossover derived from the Bolt EUV with an LFP battery and NACS port, went on sale as a 2027 model.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original Bolt EV hatchback on GM's BEV2 platform with LG Chem cells; the pack grew from 60 kWh to 66 kWh for 2020, lifting EPA range from 238 to 259 miles. All 2017-2022 cars were recalled for battery replacement.

generations.name: Refresh
generations.description: 2022 facelift with new front and rear styling, a redesigned interior, 11.5 kW onboard charging and DC fast charging made standard (still 55 kW). Production ended on 20 December 2023.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Crossover body derived from the Bolt EUV, 65 kWh LFP pack with CATL cells, 150 kW DC charging, a factory NACS port and the Equinox EV's drive unit. Built at Fairfax, Kansas from January 2026 as a single 2027 model-year run.

models.name: Bolt EUV
models.description: Longer, crossover-styled companion to the Bolt EV on the same BEV2 platform, and the first Chevrolet offered with Super Cruise. Sold for the 2022 and 2023 model years; production ended on 20 December 2023 and its body became the basis of the 2027 Bolt.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Single front-motor configuration with a 65 kWh pack, 247-mile EPA range and 55 kW DC charging.

models.name: Equinox EV
models.description: Compact electric SUV on GM's BEV3 (Ultium) platform, built in Ramos Arizpe, Mexico, and GM's best-selling EV since 2024. Every version uses an 85 kWh pack; the 2027 model year adds a built-in NACS charging port. A China-built version was shown in 2024 but never went on sale there.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched for 2024 (2LT/3LT/2RS/3RS); simplified to LT and RS for 2025 with more power, then LT 1, LT 2 and RS.

models.name: Blazer EV
models.description: Mid-size electric SUV on GM's BEV3 (Ultium) platform, built in Ramos Arizpe, Mexico since late 2023, with front-, rear- and all-wheel-drive versions plus the 615 hp SS. Production paused from December 2023 to March 2024 over software problems; the RS RWD was dropped after the 2025 model year.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with 2LT and RS trims (85 kWh AWD and 102 kWh RWD); FWD and the SS were added for 2025.

models.name: Silverado EV
models.description: Full-size electric crew-cab pickup on GM's BT1 platform with a midgate, built at Factory Zero in Detroit since 2023. It began with fleet Work Truck versions and the RST First Edition; for 2026 the RST was dropped, new drive units arrived and Standard, Extended and Max Range packs are offered across WT, LT and Trail Boss.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Same body throughout; capability changes by battery size (Standard, Extended, Max Range) and model year.

models.name: BrightDrop
models.description: Electric delivery van launched in 2021 by GM's BrightDrop unit as the EV600 / Zevo 600, joined by the shorter Zevo 400; from the 2025 model year sold through Chevrolet dealers as the Chevrolet BrightDrop 400 and 600. GM ended production at CAMI Ingersoll, Ontario, in October 2025 citing weak demand.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Ultium-based van in two lengths (400 and 600). Launched dual-motor AWD with the 20-module Max Range pack; a 14-module pack became standard for 2024 and a front-motor version arrived for 2025.

models.name: Menlo
models.description: China-only electric crossover wagon built by SAIC-GM in Wuhan from 2020, Chevrolet's first EV in China. Sales dwindled to about 100 cars in 2025, and Chevrolet stopped selling new cars in China in August 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with a 52.5 kWh pack and 110 kW motor; upgraded for 2022 to 61.1 kWh and 130 kW.

models.name: Spark EUV
models.description: Small electric SUV made by SAIC-GM-Wuling in China (the Baojun Yep Plus) and sold as a Chevrolet in Latin America, the Middle East and the Philippines from 2025; Brazilian kit assembly began in December 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rebadged Baojun Yep Plus with an LFP battery and a 75 kW motor.

models.name: Captiva EV
models.description: Compact electric SUV built by SAIC-GM-Wuling (the Wuling Starlight S) and sold as a Chevrolet in Latin America, the Middle East and the Philippines since 2025, alongside a plug-in hybrid Captiva.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rebadged Wuling Starlight S EV with a 60 kWh LFP pack and a 150 kW front motor.

legacy_notes.note: Labelled '2LT FWD' but the $34,995 price is the 2025 LT FWD price including destination (the 2024 2LT cost more). Power 213 hp / 236 lb-ft, 0-60 5.8 s and top speed 113 mph could not be sourced; 2025+ FWD is 220 hp / 242 lb-ft. 319 mi EPA and 85 kWh are correct. Mapped to the FWD variant; the legacy row was the only Chevrolet EV on the site.

gaps: Pre-2026 Chevrolet MSRPs (Spark EV, Bolt EV, Bolt EUV, 2024-2025 Equinox EV / Blazer EV) not included: could not confirm price basis (with/without destination) from a fetchable source.
Blazer EV 2026 prices from Cars.com trim listings are assumed to exclude destination (Cars.com trim listings for Silverado EV exclude it); verify against Chevrolet.
Equinox EV AWD torque not set: sources disagree (346, 348, 355 lb-ft). 2024 FWD/AWD output differed slightly from 2025+ (variant shows 2025+ figures).
Equinox EV 2026 AWD with the 19.2 kW onboard charger is rated 288 mi EPA (11.5 kW charger: 307 mi); only the latter is listed.
Silverado EV battery capacities (about 205 kWh usable for Max Range) not set: no primary source fetched. 2027 Silverado EV prices and output not found; 2027 drive units are rated 290/295 kW by EPA.
Silverado EV 2025 LT/RST Extended Range EPA range is 408 mi with the 11.5 kW charger (390 mi with 19.2 kW). 2025 RST Max Range EPA rating not found.
2026/2027 Blazer EV and Equinox EV connector: Equinox EV gets a built-in NACS port for 2027; Blazer EV 2027 connector not confirmed.

BrightDrop: 400 and 600 bodies are combined per battery/motor configuration; ranges are GM estimates (400 shown). A 2026 model-year spec (102.4 / 121 / 173.3 kWh packs, 176 / 204 / 285 mi) was published, but production ended in October 2025, so no 2026 variants are listed.

Menlo, Spark EUV, Captiva EV: no price or range in an allowed market/cycle (Menlo was NEDC-rated; Spark EUV and Captiva EV are sold in Latin America / Middle East, which have no market key). The Chinese twin Wuling Starlight S EV is rated 510 km CLTC.
Menlo exact end-of-production date not found; Wikipedia lists production to 2026 and Chevrolet ended China retail sales in August 2026.
Spark EV 2014 power: sources conflict (130 hp Wikipedia vs 104 kW EPA); left null.
Not researched for lack of web search budget: Chevrolet Sail EV / Springo (China, ~2012), Korean-market Equinox EV, and Middle East / Latin America pricing.
